terms.comment: The evening office of East and West alike. In the Byzantine rite it begins the liturgical day, and Ps. 140 (141) is its lamp-lighting psalm; in the West the Magnificat is sung at Vespers. Classical vespera is the evening itself (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Egeria, Itin. 25: et ad lucernāre jūxtā cōnsuētūdinem cotīdiānam fit
terms.comment: Egeria’s word for the evening service at Jerusalem, from lucernāris, of lamps (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Dīrigātur ōrātiō mea sīcut incēnsum in cōnspectū tuō; ēlevātiō manuum meārum sacrificium vespertīnum.
phrases.english: Let my prayer rise like incense before you, the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice.

sources: Lewis & Short: vespera · Lewis & Short: lucernaris · Lewis & Short: officium · Lewis & Short: vespertinus
